purpose: A fail-closed bijection for positions within the 365-day pharaonic Egyptian civil year. It supplies neither a default historical chronology nor hemerological judgments.

verified_claims: The civil year contains twelve 30-day months plus five days upon the year.
Four months form each of Akhet, Peret and Shemu.
The compared hemerology data contain no preserved prognoses for the five heriu-renpet days; this is not proof that every original witness omitted them.
The 365-day year drifts against the natural seasons.
The three prognosis units and their time mapping are a separate interpretive problem.
The table lists four months in each of Akhet, Peret and Shemu followed by five epagomenal days.
The later Alexandrian/Coptic leap-day reform must not be back-projected into the pharaonic 365-day model.

source_anchors.location: PDF pp.38-39 / printed pp.34-35; Plates LXXXVIII-CXXVIII on PDF pp.231-311
verified_claims: Sallier IV is a Calendar of Lucky and Unlucky Days preserved in twenty-three columns across two surviving portions.
The portion probably containing the Five Epagomenal Days is lost.
The loss of a source portion cannot be encoded as proof that the original calendar assigned no prognosis.
Selected English summaries and a facsimile do not supply a complete critical rule corpus.

calendar_model.position_contract: Zero-based year positions 0-359 map to three seasons, four months per season and thirty days per month; positions 360-364 map to heriu-renpet days 1-5.
calendar_model.year_advance_contract: Integer offsets use Euclidean division by 365 and return a signed year_delta plus the normalized position.

chronology_contract.supported_date_input: An ISO civil date already resolved under the named calendar policy and day boundary.
unsupported_profiles: Alexandrian or Coptic leap-year rules projected backward
A modern fixed month/day table treated as universal pharaonic chronology
An unnamed reign, epoch, locality, calendar policy or day boundary

hemerology_boundary.ordinary_date_prognosis: requires a separately selected and collated witness entry
hemerology_boundary.heriu_renpet_prognosis: no prognosis survives in the currently inspected main-calendar data; Sallier IV's likely epagomenal portion is lost, so historical absence is not proven
hemerology_boundary.three_part_time_mapping: not implemented; source-specific and scholarly interpretation must remain explicit

remaining_gates: Acquire a controlling chronology for each historical regime and anchor.
Acquire and collate Bakir 1966 and Leitz 1994 against the papyri.
Encode witness-specific prognosis units, damage and restorations separately.
Obtain Egyptological, Hieratic and calendrical review.
Resolve museum-image and modern-edition rights before public display.
